itemListElement.name: pWPS vs WPQR vs WPS: The Difference Explained

@graph.headline: pWPS vs WPQR vs WPS: The Difference Explained
@graph.description: A plain-language guide to the three welding procedure records — pWPS (preliminary), WPQR (the qualification record, equivalent to an ASME PQR) and WPS (the production procedure) — and how ISO and ASME differ.

mainEntity.name: Is a WPQR the same as a PQR?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — WPQR is the ISO name, PQR the ASME name, for the record of a procedure qualification test. The practical difference is where the qualified ranges are written: in the WPQR under ISO, on the WPS under ASME.

mainEntity.name: Can one WPQR support several WPS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A WPQR qualifies a range, so any number of WPS can rest on it as long as each stays inside that range. A shop usually has far more WPS than WPQRs.

mainEntity.name: Do I always need a pWPS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only when you qualify a new procedure by test. If an existing WPQR already covers the job, you write the WPS directly from it.

mainEntity.name: Where does the WPQ fit in?

acceptedAnswer.text: The WPQ qualifies the welder, not the procedure. It has its own rules for staying valid — see welder qualification validity, continuity and revalidation.
